content.title: About
content.content: Pancakes are thin, round cakes made from a liquid batter of flour, milk, eggs, and a small amount of sugar. The batter cooks quickly on a hot skillet, forming a soft, lightly golden surface. Pancakes are traditionally served with sour cream, honey, jam, berries, or simply plain.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pancakes are known worldwide: in Russia they are called “bliny”, in France “crêpes”, in Japan “okonomiyaki”.
The tradition of eating pancakes on Maslenitsa is linked to bidding farewell to winter and welcoming spring.
The largest pancake on record measured over 15 meters in diameter and was made in Russia in 2015.
Pancakes can be sweet or savory depending on batter additives and fillings.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Pancakes provide a quick source of energy thanks to their carbohydrate content.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Eggs and milk in the batter supply a modest amount of complete protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Flour and eggs are rich in B1, B2, and B6 vitamins, which support metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Milk contributes calcium and phosphorus, essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional pancakes are made with wheat flour, which can be problematic for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Pancakes can raise blood sugar quickly, so they should be consumed in moderation, especially by individuals with diabetes.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Cooking in oil increases the fat content; using a moderate amount of vegetable oil is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pancakes can be served with sour cream, honey, jam, fresh berries, cottage cheese, caviar, or meat fillings. They are also used as a base for rolls and casseroles.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked pancakes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a stack separated by parchment paper and use within 1‑2 months.
